# 1 Samuel Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 153r–153v | **Source Image:** 1SA_006_page_001.jpg, 1SA_006_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Now the ark of the LORD was in the territory of the Philistines for seven months.

**2** And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us with what we shall send it to its place."

**3** And they said, "If you are sending the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it empty, but you shall surely return to Him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be made known to you why His hand does not turn away from you."

**4** And they said, "What is the guilt offering that we shall return to Him?" And they said, "According to the number of the lords of the Philistines: five tumors of gold and five mice of gold, for one plague was upon all of you and upon your lords.

**5** And you shall make images of your tumors and images of your mice that are destroying the land, and you shall give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps He will lighten His hand from upon you and from upon your gods and from upon your land.

**6** And why should you harden your hearts as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? Was it not after He dealt severely with them that they sent them away, and they went?

**7** Now then, take and prepare one new cart and two milk cows upon which no yoke has come, and yoke the cows to the cart, but take their calves home, away from them.

**8** And take the ark of the LORD and set it upon the cart, and the articles of gold which you are returning to Him as a guilt offering, place in a box beside it. Then send it away, and let it go.

**9** And watch: if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth-shemesh, then He has done this great evil to us; but if not, then we shall know that it was not His hand that struck us — it was a chance thing that happened to us."

**10** And the men did so. They took two milk cows and yoked them to the cart and shut up their calves at home.

**11** And they set the ark of the LORD upon the cart, along with the box and the golden mice and the images of their tumors.

**12** And the cows went straight on the road, on the way to Beth-shemesh. They went along one highway, lowing as they went, and they did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the lords of the Philistines followed them to the border of Beth-shemesh.

**13** Now the people of Beth-shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley, and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.

**14** And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stopped there beside a great stone. And they split the wood of the cart and offered up the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

**15** And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, in which were the articles of gold, and they set them upon the great stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices to the LORD on that day.

**16** And the five lords of the Philistines saw it and returned to Ekron that same day.

**17** And these are the golden tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron.

**18** And the golden mice corresponded to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, from the fortified city to the village of the open country, and including the great stone upon which they set the ark of the LORD, which remains to this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.

**19** And He struck some of the men of Beth-shemesh because they had looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck seventy men of the people, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck the people with a great blow.

**20** And the men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom shall He go up from us?"

**21** And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up to you."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **6:3 — "guilt offering" (אָשָׁם)**: The Philistine priests use Israelite sacrificial terminology — the אָשָׁם is a specific category of offering in Levitical law (Leviticus 5-7) for trespass against holy things. Their awareness of this concept is noteworthy.

2. **6:6 — "harden your hearts as Egypt"**: The Philistine priests draw an explicit parallel to the Exodus narrative, warning against repeating Pharaoh's resistance. This is a remarkable narrative moment — Gentile priests invoking Israelite salvation history.

3. **6:9 — the test of the cows**: The test is elegant: nursing cows would naturally return to their calves. If they instead go toward Beth-shemesh — against every natural instinct — it proves divine causation. The Philistines design an experiment to distinguish providence from coincidence.

4. **6:12 — "lowing as they went"**: The cows go straight toward Israelite territory while lowing for their calves — obeying the divine will against their natural instinct. The detail emphasizes the supernatural nature of the ark's return.

5. **6:18 — "great stone" vs. "great meadow"**: The Leningrad Codex reads אָבֵל (abel, "meadow"), though the Qere and context suggest אֶבֶן (even, "stone"), harmonizing with the great stone of v. 14. LOGOS follows the Qere reading for clarity.

6. **6:19 — the number struck**: The MT reads "seventy men, fifty thousand men" — a notoriously difficult textual crux. The syntax is abnormal and the number implausible for a small town. LOGOS renders "seventy men," following the likely original reading, with the "fifty thousand" widely regarded as a later gloss or corruption.

7. **6:5 — "give glory" (כָבוֹד)**: The kavod wordplay continues from chapter 4: Ichabod ("no glory") gives way to the Philistines being told to "give glory" to God. The glory that departed Israel now compels homage from its captors.

— LOGOS
